questions.q: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: Air is a uniform mixture of several gases, so it is a homogeneous mixture; the other options are pure substances.

questions.q: What is the molar mass of sulphuric acid, H2SO4? (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)
How many atoms are present in 0.5 mol of oxygen gas, O2? (NA = 6.022 × 10^23 per mol)
questions.explanation: 0.5 mol of O2 is 0.5 × 6.022 × 10^23 molecules, and each molecule has 2 atoms, giving 6.022 × 10^23 atoms.

questions.q: What is the mass of nitrogen gas in 11.2 L at 273 K and 1 atm? (N = 14; molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.explanation: 11.2 L is 0.5 mol of N2, and 0.5 × 28 g/mol = 14 g.

questions.q: Which of the following contains the largest number of atoms?
questions.explanation: NH3 has 4 atoms per molecule, CO2 and H2O have 3, and O2 has 2, so 1 mol of NH3 has the most atoms.

questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of water of crystallisation in CuSO4·5H2O? (Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
What volume of 0.5 M NaOH solution contains 2 g of NaOH? (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: 2 g is 0.05 mol, and volume = 0.05 mol / 0.5 mol per L = 0.1 L = 100 mL.

questions.q: State the law of multiple proportions and illustrate it with carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide.
questions.answer: When two elements form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a simple whole-number ratio. In CO and CO2, 12 g of carbon combines with 16 g and 32 g of oxygen, a ratio of 1 : 2.
keyPoints: Fixed mass of one element, varying mass of the other
CO and CO2: 16 g and 32 g of oxygen per 12 g carbon, ratio 1:2
questions.explanation: This law was proposed by Dalton and supports the atomic theory.

questions.q: Calcium carbonate decomposes as CaCO3 → CaO + CO2. What mass of CaCO3 must be heated to obtain 11.2 L of CO2 at 273 K and 1 atm? (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16; molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.explanation: The mole ratio CaCO3 : CO2 is 1 : 1, so 0.5 mol of CaCO3 (50 g) is needed.

questions.q: How many electrons are present in a magnesium ion, Mg2+? (Atomic number of Mg = 12)
questions.explanation: A neutral Mg atom has 12 electrons; Mg2+ has lost 2, so it has 10.

questions.q: Which of the following particles has the smallest mass?
questions.explanation: An electron has a mass of about 9.1 × 10^-31 kg, nearly 1/1836 of a proton.

questions.q: What is the value of the azimuthal quantum number l for a p orbital?
questions.explanation: s, p, d and f orbitals have l = 0, 1, 2 and 3 respectively.

questions.q: How many orbitals are there in a d subshell?
questions.explanation: For l = 2 the magnetic quantum number takes 2l + 1 = 5 values.

questions.q: Which of the following electromagnetic radiations has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In order of decreasing wavelength: radio waves, microwaves, visible light, X-rays, so X-rays are shortest here.

questions.q: The energy of an electron in the nth orbit of hydrogen is -2.18 × 10^-18/n^2 J. What is its energy in the n = 2 orbit?
Which of the following ions is paramagnetic?
questions.explanation: Fe3+ is 3d5 with five unpaired electrons; Zn2+ and Cu+ are 3d10 and Sc3+ is 3d0, so all of those are diamagnetic.

questions.q: Write the ground state electronic configuration of copper (Z = 29) and explain why it is not [Ar] 3d9 4s2.
questions.answer: [Ar] 3d10 4s1. A completely filled d subshell is extra stable, so one 4s electron moves into the 3d subshell.
keyPoints: Fully filled d10 gives extra stability
Exchange energy and symmetry favour this arrangement
questions.explanation: Cu and Cr are the common exceptions to the simple filling order for this reason.

questions.q: Calculate the wavelength of light emitted when an electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 3 to n = 2. (R_H = 1.097 × 10^7 m^-1)
questions.answer: About 6.56 × 10^-7 m (656 nm), in the visible region
questions.explanation: This is the first line (H-alpha) of the Balmer series.

questions.q: Which scientist arranged elements in order of increasing atomic mass and left gaps for undiscovered elements?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev's table left gaps for elements such as gallium and germanium and predicted their properties.

questions.q: All the elements in the same period of the periodic table have the same number of
questions.explanation: The period number equals the number of occupied electron shells.

questions.q: Elements with atomic numbers 3, 11 and 19 are
questions.explanation: Lithium, sodium and potassium all have one valence electron and are group 1 alkali metals.

questions.q: Which of the following ions has the smallest radius?
questions.explanation: These ions are isoelectronic (10 electrons), and Al3+ has the highest nuclear charge, which pulls the electrons in most.

questions.q: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric?
questions.explanation: Al2O3 reacts with both acids and bases; Na2O and MgO are basic and SO2 is acidic.

questions.q: The atomic radii quoted for noble gases are unusually large compared with the elements next to them in the same period because
options: they are van der Waals radii, which are larger than covalent radii
they have more electron shells than the neighbouring elements
they have a lower nuclear charge
they have no electrons in the outermost shell
questions.explanation: Noble gases form no covalent bonds, so only van der Waals radii can be measured, and these are larger than covalent radii.

questions.q: The first ionisation enthalpy of oxygen is lower than that of nitrogen mainly because
options: in oxygen one 2p orbital holds a pair of electrons, and the repulsion makes that electron easier to remove
oxygen has a larger atomic radius than nitrogen
oxygen has a lower nuclear charge than nitrogen
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has a stable half-filled 2p3 configuration, whereas in oxygen (2p4) the paired electrons repel each other.

questions.q: State Mendeleev's periodic law and mention one achievement of his periodic table.
questions.answer: The properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses. He left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties (for example eka-aluminium, later found as gallium).
keyPoints: Predictions later confirmed, such as gallium
questions.explanation: The modern law replaced atomic mass with atomic number.

questions.q: Why do noble gases have positive electron gain enthalpy values?
questions.answer: Their valence shells are completely filled and stable, so an added electron must go into the next higher shell, which needs energy to be supplied.
keyPoints: Extra electron enters a new, higher energy shell
Energy has to be supplied, so the value is positive
questions.explanation: There is no net attraction from the nucleus for an additional electron in a new shell.

questions.q: According to the octet rule, atoms tend to have how many electrons in their outermost shell?
questions.explanation: Atoms combine to reach a stable noble gas configuration, commonly eight outer electrons.

questions.q: A covalent bond is formed by
options: complete transfer of electrons from one atom to another
sharing of electron pairs between two atoms
attraction between a metal and delocalised electrons only
questions.explanation: In a covalent bond two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

questions.q: What is the shape of a water molecule?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has two bond pairs and two lone pairs, and the lone pairs make the molecule bent with a bond angle of about 104.5 degrees.

questions.q: What is the shape of boron trifluoride, BF3?
questions.explanation: Boron has three bond pairs and no lone pair, so BF3 is sp2 hybridised and planar with 120 degree angles.

questions.q: Which of the following molecules is linear?
questions.explanation: BeCl2 has two bond pairs and no lone pairs on Be (sp hybridisation), so it is linear.

questions.q: How many sigma and pi bonds are there in ethyne, HC≡CH?
questions.explanation: Two C-H sigma bonds and one C-C sigma bond make 3 sigma; the triple bond also has 2 pi bonds.

questions.q: Among O2, O2-, O2 2- and O2+, which species has the shortest bond length?
questions.explanation: Bond orders are O2+ 2.5, O2 2, O2- 1.5 and O2 2- 1, and the highest bond order gives the shortest bond.

questions.q: Explain sp3 hybridisation using methane as an example.
questions.answer: One 2s and three 2p orbitals of carbon mix to give four equivalent sp3 hybrid orbitals directed to the corners of a tetrahedron; each overlaps with a hydrogen 1s orbital to form four C-H sigma bonds.
keyPoints: One s and three p orbitals mix
Four equivalent sp3 orbitals, 109.5 degrees apart
Overlap with hydrogen 1s gives four sigma bonds
questions.explanation: Hybridisation explains why all four C-H bonds in methane are identical.

questions.q: o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile whereas p-nitrophenol is not. Explain.
questions.answer: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, so its molecules do not associate and it is more volatile; p-nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which gives association and lower volatility.
questions.explanation: Intermolecular bonding raises the boiling point, so only the ortho isomer distils with steam.

questions.q: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.explanation: A liquid takes the shape of its container but does not change its volume.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of surface tension?
questions.explanation: Surface tension is force per unit length, so its SI unit is newton per metre.

questions.q: The vapour pressure of a liquid increases with
options: increase in surface area of the liquid
increase in volume of the container
questions.explanation: A higher temperature gives more molecules enough energy to escape, raising vapour pressure.

questions.q: According to the kinetic molecular theory, the average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to the
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy is (3/2)kT per molecule, so it depends on absolute temperature only.

questions.q: A gas occupies 1.0 L at 27 °C and constant pressure. What is its volume at 127 °C?
questions.explanation: Convert to kelvin: V2 = 1.0 × 400/300 = 1.33 L.

questions.q: A vessel contains 2 g of hydrogen and 32 g of oxygen at a total pressure of 3 atm. What is the partial pressure of hydrogen? (H2 = 2 g/mol, O2 = 32 g/mol)
questions.explanation: There is 1 mol of each gas, so the mole fraction of H2 is 0.5 and its partial pressure is 0.5 × 3 = 1.5 atm.

questions.q: State Dalton's law of partial pressures.
questions.answer: The total pressure of a mixture of non-reacting gases is the sum of the partial pressures that each gas would exert if it alone occupied the same volume at the same temperature.
keyPoints: Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure
questions.explanation: Each gas behaves independently of the others in an ideal mixture.

questions.q: Name two assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory that are not true for real gases.
questions.answer: The theory assumes that the volume of the gas molecules is negligible and that there are no attractive forces between them; in real gases both exist, especially at high pressure and low temperature.
keyPoints: Deviations are greatest at high pressure and low temperature
questions.explanation: The van der Waals equation corrects the ideal gas law for both effects.

questions.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explanation: The joule is the SI unit of energy, work and heat.

questions.q: In an adiabatic process
options: no heat is exchanged between the system and its surroundings
questions.explanation: Adiabatic means q = 0, so the change in internal energy equals the work done.

questions.q: For the isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, the change in internal energy ΔU is
questions.explanation: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, and temperature is constant.

questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion of carbon is -393.5 kJ/mol. How much heat is released when 6 g of carbon burns completely? (C = 12)
questions.explanation: 6 g is 0.5 mol, so heat released = 0.5 × 393.5 = 196.75 kJ.

questions.q: A reaction has ΔH = -40 kJ and ΔS = -100 J/K at 298 K. What is ΔG at this temperature?
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS = -40 000 - 298(-100) = -40 000 + 29 800 = -10 200 J, so the reaction is spontaneous.

questions.q: For which of the following reactions is the entropy change positive?
questions.explanation: The decomposition produces a gas from a solid, so disorder increases; the other reactions reduce the number of gas molecules.

questions.q: State Hess's law of constant heat summation.
questions.answer: The total enthalpy change for a reaction is the same whether it occurs in one step or in several steps, because enthalpy is a state function.
keyPoints: Depends only on initial and final states
Because enthalpy is a state function
questions.explanation: This lets us calculate enthalpies of reactions that cannot be measured directly.

questions.q: A reaction has a negative ΔH and a positive ΔS. Is it spontaneous at all temperatures? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes. ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, and with ΔH negative and ΔS positive both terms make ΔG negative at every temperature.
keyPoints: -TΔS is negative when ΔS is positive
So ΔG is negative at all temperatures
questions.explanation: Both the enthalpy and entropy factors favour the reaction.

questions.q: On the pH scale at 25 °C, the usual range of values for aqueous solutions is
questions.explanation: pH = 0 for 1 M strong acid and 14 for 1 M strong base, so the scale runs from 0 to 14.

questions.q: According to Arrhenius, a base produces which ion in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Arrhenius defined acids as H+ producers and bases as OH- producers in water.

questions.q: What is the value of the ionic product of water, Kw, at 25 °C?
What are the units of Kc for the reaction 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g)?
questions.explanation: Kc = [SO3]^2/([SO2]^2[O2]) has units (mol/L)^(2-3) = (mol/L)^-1, which is L/mol.

questions.q: An acetate buffer has pKa = 4.75 and a [CH3COONa]/[CH3COOH] ratio of 10. What is its pH?
questions.explanation: By the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, pH = 4.75 + log 10 = 5.75.

questions.q: A 0.1 M solution of a weak acid HA is 1% dissociated. What is the value of Ka?
What is the common ion effect? Give an example.
questions.answer: The dissociation of a weak electrolyte is suppressed when a strong electrolyte with an ion in common is added; for example, NH4Cl added to NH4OH lowers the OH- concentration.
keyPoints: Added ion is common to the weak electrolyte
Equilibrium shifts toward the undissociated form
Example: NH4Cl with NH4OH, or sodium acetate with acetic acid
questions.explanation: By Le Chatelier's principle, extra NH4+ pushes the ionisation of NH3 backwards.

questions.q: For X ⇌ Y, Kc = 4 at a certain temperature. If a mixture has [X] = 1 M and [Y] = 8 M, in which direction will the reaction proceed to reach equilibrium?
questions.answer: Backward (towards X), because Qc = 8 is greater than Kc = 4.
keyPoints: Net reaction goes from products to reactants
questions.explanation: When Qc exceeds Kc, there is too much product and the system shifts backward.

questions.q: The rusting of iron is an example of
questions.explanation: Iron loses electrons and is oxidised, forming hydrated iron(III) oxide.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of an element in its free (uncombined) state?
questions.explanation: In an elemental substance all atoms are identical, so there is no electron transfer and the oxidation number is zero.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in the ammonium ion, NH4+?
What is the oxidation number of manganese in the manganate ion, MnO4 2-?
In the reaction 2KI + Cl2 → 2KCl + I2, the iodide ion is
questions.explanation: I- loses electrons to become I2 (oxidation number -1 to 0), so it is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent.

questions.q: Which of the following species can act only as an oxidising agent and never as a reducing agent?
questions.explanation: Mn in MnO4- is already in its highest oxidation state (+7), so it can only be reduced.

questions.q: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of change in oxidation number, and illustrate with CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O.
questions.answer: Oxidation is an increase in oxidation number and reduction is a decrease. In the reaction, H2 is oxidised (0 to +1) and Cu in CuO is reduced (+2 to 0).
questions.explanation: Both processes occur together, which makes the reaction a redox reaction.

questions.q: Show that the reaction Cl2 + 2OH- → Cl- + ClO- + H2O is a disproportionation reaction.
questions.answer: Chlorine goes from 0 in Cl2 to -1 in Cl- (reduction) and to +1 in ClO- (oxidation), so the same element is both oxidised and reduced.
questions.explanation: A reaction in which one species is simultaneously oxidised and reduced is called disproportionation.

questions.q: Which element is the most abundant in the universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen makes up about 70% of the mass of the universe.

questions.q: The general outer electronic configuration of alkali metals is
questions.explanation: Alkali metals (group 1) have a single electron in the outermost s orbital.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate (sodium bicarbonate), NaHCO3.

questions.q: Milk of lime is
options: a suspension of calcium hydroxide in water
questions.explanation: Slaked lime is only sparingly soluble, and its suspension in water is called milk of lime.

questions.q: Sodium metal is manufactured commercially by
questions.explanation: In Down's process molten NaCl (with CaCl2 added to lower the melting point) is electrolysed and sodium forms at the cathode.

questions.q: Which of the following hydroxides is the strongest base?
questions.explanation: Basic character of group 2 hydroxides increases down the group, so Ba(OH)2 is strongest and Be(OH)2 is amphoteric.

questions.q: Potassium burns in excess oxygen to give the superoxide KO2, whereas lithium gives only Li2O. This is because
options: potassium has a smaller ionic radius than lithium
a large cation like K+ stabilises the large superoxide ion, but the small Li+ cannot
lithium has a higher atomic number
questions.explanation: Large anions are stabilised by large cations of low charge density, so K, Rb and Cs form superoxides.

questions.q: Write the equation for the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate and name the products.
questions.answer: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 on strong heating (about 1200 K). The products are quicklime (calcium oxide) and carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: This reaction is used industrially to make lime from limestone.

questions.q: Why is the first ionisation enthalpy of an alkaline earth metal higher than that of the alkali metal in the same period?
questions.answer: Alkaline earth atoms are smaller and have a greater nuclear charge, so the outer electron is held more strongly.
questions.explanation: For example, Mg has a higher first ionisation enthalpy than Na.

questions.q: What is the general outer electronic configuration of group 13 elements?
questions.explanation: Group 13 elements have three valence electrons, two in the s and one in the p subshell.

questions.q: Which of the following is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond has a rigid three-dimensional covalent network of sp3 carbon atoms.

questions.q: On strong heating, boric acid finally gives
questions.explanation: H3BO3 loses water to form metaboric acid HBO2 and then boron trioxide, B2O3.

questions.q: The two common oxidation states shown by group 14 elements are
questions.explanation: Group 14 elements have four valence electrons, giving +4 mainly and +2 (more stable for heavier members) through the inert pair effect.

questions.q: Which of the following oxides is neutral?
questions.explanation: CO does not react with acids or bases; CO2 and SiO2 are acidic and SnO2 is amphoteric.

questions.q: Boron trifluoride readily forms an addition compound with ammonia because
options: BF3 is a strong reducing agent
BF3 is electron-deficient and accepts the lone pair of NH3
questions.explanation: Boron in BF3 has only six electrons, so it acts as a Lewis acid and forms the coordinate adduct H3N→BF3.

questions.q: Thallium shows the +1 oxidation state more readily than +3. This is due to
questions.explanation: In the heaviest group 13 element the 6s2 pair is reluctant to take part in bonding, which stabilises the lower oxidation state.

questions.q: Mention two uses of borax.
questions.answer: Borax is used in making heat-resistant borosilicate glass and enamels, and as a flux in soldering and welding; it is also used in the borax bead test.
questions.explanation: On heating, borax gives a glassy bead of sodium metaborate and boron trioxide that dissolves metal oxides.

questions.q: Diamond is extremely hard, while graphite is soft and used as a lubricant. Explain the difference.
questions.answer: In diamond every carbon is bonded tetrahedrally to four others in a strong 3D network. In graphite carbon atoms are in layers held together by weak van der Waals forces, so the layers slide over one another.
keyPoints: Diamond: rigid 3D network of sp3 carbons
Weak forces between graphite layers allow sliding
questions.explanation: The structure explains the different mechanical properties of the two allotropes.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen, which is true only for C2H6 (ethane).

questions.q: The functional group present in alcohols is
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain a hydroxyl group (-OH) attached to a saturated carbon.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3CHO?
questions.explanation: Two carbons with an aldehyde group give ethanal (acetaldehyde).

questions.q: How many structural isomers does pentane, C5H12, have (including itself)?
questions.explanation: The isomers are pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

questions.q: Which of the following alkyl groups has the strongest +I effect?
questions.explanation: The +I effect increases with the number of alkyl groups on the carbon, so tert-butyl is strongest.

questions.q: Steam distillation is used to purify organic compounds that are
options: steam volatile and immiscible with water
questions.explanation: Such compounds, for example aniline, distil with steam at a temperature below their own boiling point and can be separated from the water.

questions.q: In Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia obtained from 1.4 g of an organic compound neutralised 20 mL of 1 M H2SO4. What is the percentage of nitrogen in the compound? (N = 14)
questions.explanation: 20 mL of 1 M H2SO4 is 0.02 mol, which neutralises 0.04 mol NH3; 0.04 × 14 = 0.56 g N, and 0.56/1.4 × 100 = 40%.

questions.q: Define homologous series and give one example.
questions.answer: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties, in which successive members differ by a -CH2- unit; example: methane, ethane, propane (alkanes).
questions.explanation: Members share a general formula and show a gradual change in physical properties.

questions.q: Explain why phenol is more acidic than ethanol.
questions.answer: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by delocalisation of its negative charge into the benzene ring through resonance, whereas the ethoxide ion has no such stabilisation and the alkyl group even destabilises it.
keyPoints: More stable conjugate base means stronger acid
questions.explanation: The more stable the conjugate base, the more easily the proton is lost.

questions.q: What is the H-C-C bond angle in ethyne, HC≡CH?
questions.explanation: Each carbon is sp hybridised, so the molecule is linear.

questions.q: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Ethane has only single bonds, whereas the others have double, triple or aromatic bonding.

questions.q: Cracking of alkanes is the process of
options: breaking larger alkane molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes by heating
questions.explanation: Heating higher alkanes at high temperature, with or without a catalyst, splits them into smaller hydrocarbons.

questions.q: In the chlorination of methane in sunlight, the step Cl2 → 2Cl• is called
questions.explanation: Initiation produces the free radicals that start the chain reaction.

questions.q: How many different monochloro structural isomers can be obtained from propane?
questions.explanation: 1-Chloropropane and 2-chloropropane are possible, because propane has two kinds of hydrogen.

questions.q: Nitration of toluene (methylbenzene) gives mainly
questions.explanation: The methyl group is an activating, ortho/para directing substituent.

questions.q: Ethene reacts with cold dilute alkaline potassium permanganate solution to give
questions.explanation: Baeyer's reagent adds two hydroxyl groups across the double bond, and the purple colour is discharged.

questions.q: Write the equation for the preparation of methane by heating sodium acetate with soda lime.
questions.explanation: The carboxylate group is lost as carbonate, leaving the methyl group to take a hydrogen.

questions.q: Why is the staggered conformation of ethane more stable than the eclipsed conformation?
questions.answer: In the staggered form the C-H bonds on the two carbons are as far apart as possible, so there is minimum repulsion (torsional strain); in the eclipsed form they are closest, giving the highest repulsion.
keyPoints: Eclipsed: bond pairs closest, maximum torsional strain
questions.explanation: The lower energy of the staggered form means ethane spends most of its time in it.
